references.text: God calls Bezalel by name and fills him with His Spirit, with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge to perform artistic work. This is the original appointment referred to in Exodus 38:22.
Moses announces to the children of Israel that the Lord has called Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with God's Spirit to lead the work on the tabernacle.
Bezalel and Oholiab, together with all skilled men, begin the work on the sanctuary according to the Lord's command.
Bezalel makes the ark of the covenant, which is part of the work he carried out according to the Lord's command through Moses.
First Chronicles gives the genealogy of Bezalel: son of Uri, son of Hur, who was the son of Caleb and Ephrath.
The bronze altar that Bezalel made is mentioned in connection with Solomon's worship at Gibeon.
Calling and completion: Shows the connection between God's selection of Bezalel and his actual execution of the work.
Call and obedience: Confirms that Bezalel's work was a direct result of God's specific call in 31:2.
Unity in obedience: Links Bezalel's individual leadership with the people's collective obedience to God's command.
Hierarchy in obedience: Connects Bezalel's production with Moses' setup to show comprehensive obedience.
Completion of the work: Confirms that Bezalel's work was part of the total obedience from the entire people.
Genealogical confirmation: Confirms Bezalel's lineage from Hur and his place in the tribe of Judah.
